findings.summary: Every drain start now writes a records-only commit, even when nothing changed
findings.evidence: Drain-start duties are always due at a drain start, so each drain commits one sweep record. Before, a drain over unchanged records committed nothing: drain.rs changed its assertion from `fx.head() == head` to `assert_only_a_duty_pass_since`. The cost is documented in the CHANGELOG and hestia.md. A simpler option would record a drain-start pass only when a duty changed something or failed, though last-run tracking then needs another signal.

findings.summary: A sweep inside the cadence records an empty report, which `athena hestia last` then shows
findings.evidence: An explicit sweep now commits a full (non-duty-pass) report even when no duty was due. `last_sweep` returns the newest full sweep, so a reading-rule or keep-rule finding from an earlier sweep is replaced by an empty report until that duty is due again. The request asks that a second sweep runs none. Carrying forward the newest open findings of each duty, or skipping empty sweeps in `last`, would keep them visible.

findings.summary: `athena status` now fails if counting landings fails
findings.evidence: `crate::code_health::landings(&self.git, &head)?` uses `?`, while the code-health section next to it uses `.ok()`. A git error while counting landings would stop the whole status view instead of leaving the duties section empty.

findings.summary: Drain-start duties are never overdue by age
findings.evidence: A duty that runs every drain start and has run once never shows OVERDUE, however long it has been since the last drain. This is documented and matches its cadence, but an operator cannot see from status that drains have stopped.

findings.summary: In this snapshot the dev-profile athena-core build used an out-of-date athena-data artifact
findings.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core a_sweep_runs_each_due_duty` failed with 'no `DutyPass` in `records`' while the source has it, and `cargo build -p athena-data` reported the artifact as up to date. This is likely left over from Athena's fails-without run in the shared target dir; it is a snapshot environment problem, not a code defect. Overriding the build settings with `--config` was denied, and I stopped there. The `--release` runs passed.

summary: I recommend passing this change. It does what was asked. `DUTIES` in hestia.rs and a new section 13 table in docs/design/hestia.md list the six duties: error review and evidence labels every drain start, code health every landing, design review and keep rule every 10 landings, reading-rule refusals every 5 landings. Each row names Hestia's sweep as owner and says where the duty runs. Drain starts, landings and `athena hestia sweep` all go through one `execute_duties` path. It runs only the duties that are due and records each run in the sweep record's new optional `duty_pass` field, with the occasion and the landing total at that time. `athena status` (text and JSON) now shows each duty with its last run, next due point and an OVERDUE mark. One setup problem: in this snapshot the dev-profile athena-core build failed because it linked an out-of-date athena-data build artifact, although the source has the new types. Overriding the build settings with `--config` was denied, so I did not retry that way. I ran the athena-core tests with `--release` instead (separate artifacts), and all the new tests and the 81 existing hestia tests pass. fmt, clippy and the full test suite pass in Athena's recorded CI run for this commit. The extra changed files are test adjustments and supporting code the change needs. The weaker points are all minor: every drain start now adds a small records-only commit, a sweep inside the cadence records an empty report, and status now fails if it cannot count landings.
